To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N-terminal auto-inhibitory domain regulates the catalytic VY loop of Slingshot phosphotases by modulating the stability of the phosphate leaving group and that the dissociation of the N-terminal auto-regulatory domain upon F-actin and neuregulin binding activates Slingshot2 phosphatases in vitro and in vivo, respectively.

1) the N-terminal domain inhibits Slingshot2 phosphatase activity via modulating the stability of the product leaving group, 2) F-actin relieves this inhibition by dissociating the N-terminal domain, and 3) the dissociation of the N-terminal domain is the structural basis for the activation of Slingshot by F-actin.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified an auto-inhibitory and an activation mechanism of Slingshot phospho-tyrosine phosphatase, which is important for the regulation of cytoskeleton dynamics in various cellular contexts.

the N-terminal structural elements of Slingshot are auto-inhibitory and can be dissociated upon F-actin and neuregulin binding, which leads to the exposure of the catalytic site and activation of Slingshot.
the auto-inhibition of the phosphatases is relieved by the binding of the F-actins, which results in the activation of the phosphatatic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the N-terminal auto-inhibitory domain of Slingshots regulates the stability of a leaving group during catalysis by affecting the pK(a) of the catalytic Asp361 in the VYD loop, and F-actin activates Slingshots by relieving the auto-inhibition through large conformational rearrangements in the phosphatase domains.

the allosteric activation mechanism of Slingshot by F-actin and the N-terminal domain is a general mechanism that applies to all human Slingshots, and this activation is required for Slingshot to function properly in cells.
